current.title: The Coldest Place In The Universe Isn't In Space (3 Charts)
current.hook: The Coldest Place In The Universe Isn't In Space
current.closing: The universe's coldest place also has the best view.
current.question: Could you survive one second at absolute zero? Guess below.

segments.say: Room temperature is about 293 Kelvin. Deep space itself sits at 2.7 Kelvin, warmed slightly by leftover heat from the Big Bang. One nebula, 5,000 light-years away, is even colder than that.

segments.topic: Boomerang Nebula vs. NASA's Cold Atom Lab
segments.say: NASA built something colder. Its Cold Atom Lab, on the space station, chills atoms to under 100 picokelvin -- a billionth of a billionth of a degree above zero. That's a billion times colder than deep space.

segments.topic: how far away the coldest known spots really are
segments.say: The Boomerang Nebula sits 5,000 light-years away, about 30 quadrillion miles. NASA's freezer is 250 miles straight up. The coldest place in the known universe is orbiting right over your head.
